content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines introduction to web apis as part of building apis with django. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: What an API is; REST architectural concepts; Resources and representations; HTTP methods and status codes; When to return JSON instead of HTML. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: What an API is
items.text: An API contract specifies resources, methods, body validation, authentication, permissions, status codes, pagination, versioning and error formats. JSON transport alone does not make an API safe or complete.

items.title: REST architectural concepts
items.text: For REST architectural concepts, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Resources and representations
items.text: For Resources and representations, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: HTTP methods and status codes
items.text: GET is intended to retrieve data and should be safe from business-state mutation; POST is commonly used for state-changing form actions. API PUT/PATCH/DELETE semantics depend on the resource contract and must be enforced server-side.

items.title: When to return JSON instead of HTML
items.text: When to return JSON instead of HTML crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
